item.title: In 1969, a Nevada man built a desert home from junk; today, Thunder Mountain is a free attraction
item.description: Thunder Mountain Monument in Nevada features sculptures created from discarded materials by Frank Van Zant. This unique roadside attraction developed from his personal vision to honor Native American history. After a fire in 1983, the site faced preservation challenges until it was recognized as a historic site in 1992. The monument is maintained today with visitor donations and a caretaker's assistance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: David Gilmour sold his guitars for $21.5 million to fund climate change and nature protection work
item.description: In June 2019, David Gilmour sold over 120 guitars, significantly benefitting ClientEarth with the proceeds. Among them was the iconic 1969 Fender Stratocaster, which achieved a record sale price. These funds were dedicated to advancing environmental law initiatives aimed at combatting climate change. This remarkable auction intertwined rock legacy and ecological activism, illustrating Gilmour's commitment to fostering a sustainable future through music.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rihanna’s foundation teamed up with bicycle company to help girls in Malawi get to school
item.description: In an inspiring collaboration, Rihanna's Clara Lionel Foundation has teamed up with Ofo to enhance educational access for girls in Malawi through the 1 KM Action initiative. This initiative not only provides bicycles but also offers scholarships, alleviating the burdens of travel and educational expenses. Following the partnership announcement, the first bicycles arrived, significantly facilitating school attendance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jamie Oliver’s cooking programme began in 2008; by 2024, his food education work had reached 115,000+ people
item.description: Jamie Oliver's Ministry of Food, established in 2008, has made significant strides in promoting culinary skills across communities. By March 2024, it successfully engaged over 115,000 participants through school and community-based initiatives. The program not only focuses on delivering practical cooking techniques but also aims at fostering healthier dietary choices for families.

item.title: Russian strikes kill 12 in Ukraine after Trump announces diesel deal with Putin
item.description: A recent barrage of Russian airstrikes in Zaporizhzhia claimed at least 12 lives, including those of children. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy denounced a fresh diesel agreement forged by Donald Trump with Russia, highlighting concerns that such deals could fuel the persistent conflict in Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized that relaxing sanctions may encourage further military actions from Russia, underscoring the intricate and precarious nature of the current geopolitical landscape.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: A hospital worker’s $15.99 Goodwill find was identified as a Le Pho painting worth up to $80,000
item.description: An occupational therapist found a painting for $15.99 at Goodwill while shopping to relieve stress. Notably, the piece was valued significantly higher during an appraisal on Antiques Roadshow. Fine-art expert Betty Krulik identified it as a work by Vietnamese artist Le Pho. The appraisal revealed that similar artworks could sell for between $60,000 and $80,000 at auction. This exceptional find highlights the importance of expert evaluations in determining art value.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How a Martha Stewart-backed centre is rethinking elderly care
item.description: Established by Martha Stewart, the Martha Stewart Center for Living at Mount Sinai Hospital is dedicated to transforming the landscape of elderly healthcare. Through its focus on holistic well-being and specialized programs, older adults benefit from improved health outcomes, including reduced emergency visits and shorter hospitalizations. Furthermore, the center prioritizes educating healthcare professionals in geriatric practices, reinforcing a commitment to effectively support our ageing community.

item.title: Bloomberg's $1B gift to Johns Hopkins made medical tuition free for families earning under $300K
item.description: In a groundbreaking move, Johns Hopkins University revealed a $1 billion contribution from Bloomberg Philanthropies to significantly improve financial assistance for graduate students. This generous funding extends free tuition to medical students from households earning under $300,000, while those from families with incomes up to $175,000 can access support for both tuition and living expenses.

item.title: Renée Zellweger’s renovated 10-acre Topanga ranch returns to market for $7.995 million
item.description: Renée Zellweger's stunning Topanga ranch, acquired in 2015 and beautifully renovated, has hit the market for nearly $8 million. Spanning almost 10 acres, this Spanish-style estate boasts breathtaking mountain views and exclusive hiking trails. Previously sold for $6.4 million in 2021, the property is perfect for those seeking tranquility in Southern California, featuring an infinity-edge pool and meticulously landscaped outdoor areas, appealing to buyers looking for space and luxury.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: 21-year-old Mexican innovator turns waste into electricity while cleaning polluted water with microbial fuel cells
item.description: Maritza Sanchez, hailing from Cuautlancingo, Mexico, is pioneering the development of microbial fuel cells aimed at tackling severe local pollution challenges. Her initiative, Aquayac Energy, focuses on generating sustainable electricity while also purifying the heavily contaminated Atoyac River. By 2027, Sanchez intends to create 50 operational fuel cells, enhancing energy accessibility and promoting water quality.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jerry Rice’s former Bay Area mansion returns to market for $35M
item.description: NFL Hall of Famer Jerry Rice's mansion in Atherton, California has been listed for sale at $35 million. The mansion spans 12,520 square feet and includes six bedrooms along with 11 bathrooms. The property has unique features like a gym and a wine cellar, reflecting Rice's attention to detail. This estate was originally built in the early 2000s and has changed ownership since Rice sold it.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Scientists planted 40,000 seedlings in Yosemite; 3 years later, meadow is still losing carbon
item.description: Scientists planted 40,000 native sedge seedlings in Yosemite National Park's Tuolumne Meadows to restore soil damaged by sheep grazing over a century ago. After three years, researchers found improvements in soil organic matter, but the meadow continued to lose more carbon than it gained. Scientists estimate that full recovery could take 25 to 50 years.

item.title: Mine water treatment by-product ochre is being used to stabilise contaminated soil
item.description: A site in Chester, previously contaminated with lead and asbestos, is undergoing remediation to enable new apartments. Ochre from the Deerplay mine water treatment scheme is stabilising the contaminated soil on site. This approach allows for the safe management of contaminants while preparing the area for redevelopment. The project aims to construct 126 new apartments and support local regeneration efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida restored a degraded oyster reef in 2018; density rose to 91 per sq m in six months and 244 by year five
item.description: Florida’s Lone Cabbage Reef, once a vibrant oyster habitat, faced severe decline before restoration efforts. Researchers rebuilt the reef in 2018 using dolomite limestone to create suitable surfaces for oyster larvae. Subsequent studies documented significant increases in oyster populations over five years, reaching densities of 244 oysters per square metre. The restoration benefited local fisheries, generating substantial economic impact and employment opportunities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Boy Honoured For Fire Alert: Carter Hicks spots smoking trailer; fire crew hails his quick action
item.description: Carter Hicks, an observant eight-year-old, spotted smoke billowing from a camper trailer and quickly alerted local residents, sparking action from the Blooming Grove Volunteer Fire Department. Honoring his bravery, the department presented him with a patch and a Certificate of Recognition. This incident not only underscores the vital role of community vigilance but also demonstrates how young citizens can play an essential part in ensuring public safety.
